title: Regular Arithmetic Functions, Volume I. Theory, Applications, Examples
summary: This is the first of two volumes on regular arithmetic functions, and an introduction to their theory. A regular arithmetic function (RAF) is a kernel whose properties come from a single defining equation. Let $G(n,k)$ be a function of two integer variables with $G(n,n)\neq 0$, and for each $β$ define a sequence $(a_k)$ by $\sum_{k\le n} a_k G(n,k)=n^{-β}$, solved rank by rank with nothing to assume and no convergence to establish. Then $G$ is regular when the partial sums $\sum_{k\le n} a_k$ change behaviour at one exponent. Below it they reproduce the forced rate, above it they absorb it.…
